technical-summary: Made pi-mcp-adapter version checking fail-closed: apply_mcp_exclusive_patch now rejects patching when the adapter version is missing or outside the supported caret range, instead of only logging an advisory warning. Added a version-matrix + idempotency + fail-closed test suite for the patch. Added a unit test proving isolated-job worker environments (_replacement_environment) never write into the caller's native ~/.pi durable config, closing out PI01 and PI04's remaining validation gaps. Also audited and cleaned up plan items MI08, MC03, HA01, HA02, PI01, PI04, OP03, RU02, RU03, RU04 against current code state: fixed stale dependency/file references, narrowed RU03's scope to reflect that OpenCode-side mcp_format consolidation is already done, folded RU04's ownership-boundary doctrine into HA01/HA02 and deleted it as redundant.
user-summary-candidate: Pi's MCP-exclusive isolation patch now refuses to apply on unsupported adapter versions instead of silently warning, with test coverage confirming isolated agent jobs never touch your native Pi config.

technical-summary: MA22: removed the universal reconcile_provider/reconcile_all_providers functions from providers_api's public export surface and from the ag-providers-mgmt MCP tool declarations (providers.yaml + providers_mcp.py), now that MA22's blockers (SH07, MA17) are complete. commands/launch.py's on-launch reconciliation already called services.lifecycle directly (the retained private composition path) -- only its stale comment referencing MCP availability needed updating. Updated test_mcp_component_servers.py to assert the tools are absent. While revalidating MA09/MA17's boundary criteria, found and fixed one regression: agents_gateway_session_dispatch.py imported SurfaceHint directly from providers.contracts.session_surface instead of the sanctioned providers_api re-export. Also reviewed and closed out OP03 (removed per decision) and documented target-solution proposals for MC03 (MCP diagnostics design) and MI08 (test-construction approach using AG's own install/CLI capabilities).
user-summary-candidate: Removed the last public/MCP-exposed universal provider-reconcile API now that its dependencies are satisfied, and fixed a component-boundary leak in the agents gateway.

technical-summary: Fixed two bugs in refresh_harness_config_if_installed found while investigating RU02: (1) it always returned True once a harness CLI was detected on PATH, even when the actual materialize/reload-marker steps raised and were caught -- now returns an honest success/failure boolean, fixed in both pi and opencode install modules. (2) project_components.py's attach_harness_refresh called this function a second time after every install/enable/disable/uninstall, duplicating work the harness's own component-lifecycle event subscription (runtime/harness/__init__.py) already performs synchronously -- removed the redundant call; attach_harness_refresh now reports harness availability via a lightweight read-only check instead. Also built the smallest viable MCP diagnostics slice for MC03 (user confirmed hitting -32001 in practice): foundation/mcp/diagnostics.py's probe_mcp_server spawns a configured MCP server via the existing supervised_process primitive, completes the MCP initialize handshake, and reports ok/phase/elapsed_ms/exit_status/error without leaking argv/env -- wired as a new diagnose_mcp_servers tool on the existing ag-session-mgmt MCP server rather than a new subsystem, per explicit direction to keep this minimal and extensible later only if needed.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed a harness-config-refresh bug that silently misreported success and did the refresh twice on every component change, and added a minimal MCP server preflight-diagnostics tool to help debug generic MCP startup failures.

technical-summary: Removed the CLI visibility feature (cli_visibility/set_cli_visibility tools, hide_thinking_block/hide_tool_use settings) entirely as superseded by the new managed-harness topology. Investigation found it was already partly non-functional: hide_tool_use wrote audiagenticHideToolUse into Pi's settings.json but nothing in the current templates ever read it (a leftover from a removed embedded/forked-Pi patch mechanism), and OpenCode had zero support for either setting -- OpenCode's install path has no ui.* handling and no plugin/extension templates at all, so the live-reload-notification mechanism (reload-request.json polled by Pi's footer.ts) this feature depended on was Pi-only to begin with. Deleted session_visibility.py; removed the tools/settings/error-codes/reload-reason across session_api.py, session_mcp.py, session.yaml, pi/install/config.py, pi.yaml, reload.py, and updated all affected tests plus the stale materialized SYSTEM.md artifact checked into the repo root.
user-summary-candidate: Removed the CLI thinking/tool-block visibility toggle feature -- it was already broken for tool-block hiding and never worked on OpenCode, a leftover from the old embedded-harness design.

technical-summary: Traced the origin of the earlier hide_tool_use dead-config finding to commit e649112d (PI01, 2026-07-23), which deleted patches.py/patches_mcp_progress.py/patches_mcp_register.py -- ad-hoc regex patches into the Pi npm package's own source -- in favor of config-driven resolution, but left orphaned config and a dead helper behind. Removed lockdown.block_builtin_commands from pi.yaml (its patch, _patch_slash_commands/_patch_interactive_mode, is gone; the remaining no_skills/no_prompt_templates/no_context_files lockdown keys are still real, functioning Pi CLI flags, confirmed via runtime/harness/pi/runner/command.py, and were kept). Removed the now-fully-unused _audiagentic_pkg_dir helper from constants.py (its only caller, patches.py, is gone). Explicit decision recorded: no more source patches into third-party harness packages going forward. Created PI05 to track validating two behavior changes the deleted patches used to prevent (Windows OAuth callback-server EACCES port-bind noise in pi-mcp-adapter, and Pi's native update-notification UI reappearing) since those have no config to clean up -- they're accepted-but-unverified regressions, not dead config.
user-summary-candidate: Cleaned up orphaned Pi harness config and a dead helper function left over from last week's removal of third-party source patches, and filed a follow-up to verify two related behavior changes are acceptable.

technical-summary: RU03: consolidated Pi's independent mcp_format.py read/write/remove implementation onto the shared foundation/mcp/json_format.py projection, matching the pattern OpenCode's mcp_format.py already used. Kept the Pi-specific full-rebuild path (build_pi_mcp_dict, lifecycle/settings fields) as the one legitimate per-provider difference, mirroring OpenCode's own build_opencode_mcp_dict precedent. Removed the fully redundant 1:1 forwarding wrapper functions (mcp_config_path/read_mcp_config/write_mcp_config/remove_mcp_config) from both pi/install/__init__.py and opencode/install/__init__.py -- confirmed zero other callers before deleting. runtime/harness/__init__.py's facade now dispatches to each provider's mcp_format module directly; its own public API is unchanged.
user-summary-candidate: Consolidated Pi's MCP config read/write logic onto the same shared code OpenCode already uses, removing a duplicate implementation and a layer of pass-through wrapper functions.

technical-summary: HA03 slice 1: unified the ~95%-duplicated build_global_context implementation from runtime/harness/{pi,opencode}/runner/__init__.py into one harness-agnostic run_common.build_global_context(harness_type, ...). Consolidated two separate missing-model error codes (CFG-HCFG-009/011) into one, and replaced ad-hoc per-harness CLI-presence checks with one generic RES-HRNRUN-001 check via harness_cli_available(harness_type), now run before any rig work starts (previously only OpenCode failed fast; Pi failed later). The only remaining per-harness behavior is Pi's extra agent_home/agent_dir/agent_bin fields (needed by its interactive launch, not yet migrated). Added 5 new unit tests covering both harness types plus the missing-CLI and missing-model error paths, since no existing test exercised build_global_context's real implementation (only facade-level dispatch was tested). This is slice 1 of HA03, a new item capturing the user's direction to eliminate harness-specific code from runtime/harness beyond generic session/environment/logging concerns, routing actual CLI launch mechanics through the same providers mechanism ACP/execution already use.
user-summary-candidate: Removed duplicated harness-launch setup code between Pi and OpenCode, unifying it into one shared implementation with new test coverage.

technical-summary: Fixed a provider->runtime.harness dependency boundary violation introduced by HA03 slice 2: components/providers/adapters/pi/interactive.py was importing runtime.harness.resolution.harness_cli_available and runtime.harness.pi.install.constants.load_pi_config, both forbidden for the providers platform component (caught by the existing test_provider_runtime_boundary.py architecture guard). Replaced with providers' own existing require_executable helper (adapters/cli.py, already used elsewhere for the same PATH-probing job) and a self-contained load_pi_config reading the same pi.yaml via foundation.config.load_layered_config + foundation.paths.package.PACKAGE_ROOT, mirroring the identical pattern already used in adapters/pi/hooks.py. Removed the now-unnecessary RES-PIRUN-003 error-resolution registration since require_executable raises its own established EXT-PROVCLI-001 code instead. Updated test mocks to match.
user-summary-candidate: Fixed a component-boundary violation in the new Pi interactive-launch code, reusing existing provider-owned helpers instead of reaching into runtime internals.

technical-summary: Audited the two remaining MA (managed-config-consistency) plan items. MA34 (comprehensive Docker e2e capability-matrix + negative-path tests) was found already fully implemented -- tests/integration/providers/test_managed_config_capability_matrix_e2e.py (635 lines, 64 tests, collection-verified) and its Dockerfile already exist and cover every step the item specified, including the motivating hooks_format.py corruption defect, which is confirmed already fixed (RV713). Marked complete. MA35 (recipe-backed provider execution resolution) had a stale premise -- the declarative recipe system it proposed building already exists in production (base_runner.py execution: blocks, 7 of 18 providers fully recipe-driven with no adapter.py). Surveyed all 18 provider adapters and found real remaining scope: qwen and copilot each carry a hand-written adapter.py that is byte-for-byte dead-duplicate of their already-declared execution: block; pi's declared execution: block is a landmine (would reintroduce the SH21 prompt-newline-loss bug if ever reached, since it lacks a stdin-delivery option adapter.py's real fix depends on). Rewrote MA35's description/steps/files to the narrower, evidence-backed real scope: delete the two dead adapters (with test rewrites), add a prompt-delivery: stdin schema field, and document the adapter-vs-recipe split. Left MA35 pending -- real implementation work remains, not done in this pass.
user-summary-candidate: Closed out one MA item that was already secretly done, and rewrote the other's plan with concrete, verified findings instead of a stale premise.

technical-summary: Fixed RES-PREC-001 during bootstrap: operate_provider_surfaces now catches exceptions when a provider has no implementation for the generated-surfaces family. Instead of crashing the surfaces observer, it returns a GeneratedSurfaceResult with ok=False and error_code=RES-PREC-001. This prevents subscriber errors on lifecycle.component.installed events for providers like aider that declare generated-surfaces but lack an implementation.
user-summary-candidate: Bootstrap no longer crashes when provider has unimplemented surface family

technical-summary: Added MCP propagation policy validation to recipe tests. Management MCPs (propagate: audiagentic) must NOT appear in harness mcp.json — they are internal to AUDiaGentic. Fixed test_harness_user_path which incorrectly asserted ag-planning-mgmt was present; it should assert ag-planning is present and ag-planning-mgmt is absent.
user-summary-candidate: MCP propagation: management servers excluded from harness config

technical-summary: HA04: unified provider launch onto one intent-based mechanism. (1) Contract: one ProviderLaunch(executable,args,environment) in foundation/transports replacing the byte-identical AcpLaunch+InteractiveLaunch dupes (AcpLaunch kept as alias). (2) build_launch_spec: shared spec builder with a frozen two-axis vocabulary (runtime context tokens + config->flag algebra: enum/value/repeat-value/boolean-flags); make_cli_runner refactored onto it. (3) Dispatch: resolve_launch_builder(provider, intent) where intent in {execute, interactive, agent} -- caller picks intent, harness assembles its own transports/channels (caller never names a transport); one _adapter_hook collapsed the former 5 near-identical loaders. (4) Capability: descriptor.launches = {intent:{interaction:[...],observability:[...]}}, a queryable role-based channel surface (in describe_provider), fail-closed source of truth. (5) Removed Pi harness customization per user directive: deleted footer.ts (reload UI) + follow_up_actions.ts (vestigial -- its executor module was already deleted), the --extension injection, extension materialization, settings.json extensions list; Pi now launches stock (only the MCP surface's adapter remains, to deliver AG's MCP servers). (6) Simplified pi/interactive.py (tools.mode enum replacing 3 overlapping booleans; dropped dead sandbox/custom_header/extensions.load/extra_flags knobs; removed a broken startup Tools line reading the wrong config namespace). (7) OpenCode interactive is now a declarative recipe (deleted opencode/interactive.py). (8) Deleted dead qwen/copilot adapter.py duplicates (byte-identical to their execution: recipes); tests rewritten to the recipe path. Full providers+harness+agents unit suites green.
user-summary-candidate: Unified how AUDiaGentic launches AI CLIs into one clean mechanism where callers pick an intent (execute/interactive/agent) and each harness decides how to fulfil it, and stopped AUDiaGentic from injecting custom UI code into the Pi CLI.
